🔊📣 DO YOU KNOW WHAT AUSALERT IS? 🔊📣

AusAlert is an emergency warning system that uses the latest technology to send alerts directly to compatible mobile devices during disasters. It helps keep Australian communities informed, protecting lives and property.

Today phones, tablets, smartwatches will be alerted at 1:30pm in the NT. Check out our slides to find out everything you need to know!

🗞️ 🗞️ MEDIA RELEASE 🗞️ 🗞️

Workers will now face enormous pressure as they attempt to implement new Child Protection laws within an already overstretched workforce and without any additional funding. 

The sector has consistently warned that meaningful reform requires investment in prevention, early intervention, workforce capacity and culturally appropriate services—not simply changes to legislation.

Since these laws were introduced, workers, unions, Aboriginal community-controlled organisations, legal experts and community service providers have raised genuine concerns about the impact they will have on vulnerable children, families and the frontline workforce.

Those concerns have been reinforced by the draft recommendations of the Country Liberal Party-commissioned Webb-Shanahan Review, which demonstrate that the issues affecting child safety lie within the department's operations, not the legislation itself.

Rather than listening to those concerns, the CLP Government rammed through dangerous laws and went even further by labelling workers in the sector as "morally bankrupt."

Unions NT Secretary Erina Early said the comments were offensive, reckless and an insult to every worker who has dedicated their career to protecting Territory children.

#UnionsNT #ChildProtection #NTPol #SupportWorkers #TerritoryWorkers

Our hospital workers deserve better. A recent survey by the ANMFNT shows 40 per cent of workers are seeing repeated abuse and violence in their workplace. These are the people who care for you when you or a loved one are most unwell.  We are calling on everyone to join us in creating urgent change. 

Come along to the ANMFNT headquarters in Coconut Grove to hear more. 

Campaign Launch Date: Monday 20 July 2026 
Time: 10:00 am 
Venue: ANMF NT Office, 16 Caryota Court, Coconut Grove.

🗞️ 🗞️ MEDIA RELEASE 🗞️ 🗞️

The Australian Nursing and Midwifery Federation Northern Territory (ANMF NT) is calling for urgent action to eliminate workplace violence and aggression against nurses and midwives, launching its Stop Workplace Violence and Aggression campaign on 20 July 2026.

Every day, nurses and midwives across the Northern Territory face verbal abuse, threats, intimidation and physical assault while caring for the community. ANMF NT says violence should never be accepted as "part of the job."

Recent ANMF NT member surveys highlight the scale of the problem:

· 57% of respondents experienced workplace violence or aggression, with 9% of respondents facing these events daily.
· Only half of the respondents feel safe at work
· 40% see the same violent behaviours occur repeatedly in the same workplaces.
· 37% report delayed or inadequate responses.
· Of the 40% of nurses and midwives who reported their incidents, almost 60% said nothing happens afterwards.

More results from the ANMF NT members survey will be released on July 20 at the campaign launch. 
Join us and others. 
Campaign Launch Date: Monday 20 July 2026 
Time: 10:00 am 
Venue: ANMF NT Office, 16 Caryota Court, Coconut Grove.

#sickofit #ntnurses #unionsNT #UnityNT #solidarity #ANMFNT
